solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Skin condition irritates husband covering centre of worst area

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece goes around another
the centre of a word is its middle letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to nettle is to annoy or irritate
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
the middle letter of the five-letter word
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone's skin trouble is flaring up, and their husband is covering the worst-affected patch.
explanation.walkthrough: NETTLES and H run together as NETTLESH, and that string wraps around R plus A, giving NETTLE-RA-SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettle rash is the everyday name for urticaria, an itchy skin eruption like the sting of a nettle.

clue.text: Vulgar supporter turned up before start of final

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something upward makes it read from bottom to top
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a fan supports a team or performer
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A crude football fan rises from their seat just before the final kicks off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' places the reversed supporter ahead of F. Naff is British slang for tacky or in poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tasteless, tacky or lacking style, close to vulgar in the sense of crude or common.

clue.text: Turtle avoiding soft ground

indicators.note: to avoid something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: a terrapin is a small freshwater turtle
P, for piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A turtle picks its way carefully, keeping off the muddy patches of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical marking piano, meaning soft; take it out of TERRAPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain means an area of land considered for its physical features, the same as ground in a landscape sense.

clue.text: A nobly dutiful, awfully rich and generous woman

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly and messed up, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A dutiful aristocrat who is also extremely wealthy and openhanded to others.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a description of a noblewoman, which is apt, but 'awfully' is the anagram signal, not an intensifier for 'rich'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Bountiful, from a character in an 18th-century comedy, names a wealthy woman known for charitable, often showy, generosity.

clue.text: Look at section of pleasure garden

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from a larger whole, so the letters come from inside the words

blocks.note: found running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An invitation to admire one corner of a formal ornamental garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span the end of 'pleasure' and the start of 'garden'.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to gaze at it attentively, a formal synonym of look at.

clue.text: Stone rich wife dropped under the table

indicators.note: something dropped is let go and left behind, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
a synonym for rich
W is the abbreviation for wife; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A wealthy wife, weighed down with drink, has slid off her chair and under the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the table' looks like the drunk wife's resting place, but it is the definition, meaning done covertly. A stone is a British unit of body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Deals done under the table are secret and furtive, so the phrase works adjectivally for sly, covert behaviour.

clue.text: Briefly obstruct alliance

indicators.note: made brief means cut short, so the final letter is lopped off

blocks.note: to block is to obstruct; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A quick attempt to thwart a coalition of nations.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the final K from BLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of countries or parties united by a common political interest, a kind of alliance.

clue.text: Girl – Lynn, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: a girl's first name
second meaning: the first name of a famous bearer of that surname

explanation.walkthrough: Loretta Lynn was an American country music singer, so 'Lynn, perhaps' points to her first name; 'perhaps' marks her as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Loretta is a female given name, and the best-known Loretta is the country star Loretta Lynn.

clue.text: Fruit, kind in middle of tiers

indicators.note: the middle of an odd-length word is its single central letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: clement means merciful or kind
taken as written
the central letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: Fruit of a particular kind set out in the centre of a tiered display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a container signal but is simply IN, taken literally between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A clementine is a small, sweet citrus fruit, a hybrid related to the tangerine and mandarin orange.

clue.text: Support for logs in sack by track

blocks.note: to sack someone is to fire them
to dog is to follow or track

explanation.surface: A frame for carrying logs, stowed in a sack beside a woodland track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag and 'track' like a path, but both are verbs: dismiss and follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog, also called an andiron, is a metal stand in a fireplace on which burning wood is laid.

clue.text: Compel injured fencer to receive oxygen

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
receiving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An order that a wounded fencer be given oxygen on the piste.
explanation.walkthrough: The O is taken into the fencer's letters and the whole lot is then shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforce something is to make it happen by force or authority, so compel is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Honest description of boringly conventional blonde?

definitions.note: a whimsical phrase rather than a straight synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: above board, without cheating
second meaning: a pale-haired person who is also dull and old-fashioned, read word by word

explanation.walkthrough: Fair means light-haired and square means stuffily conventional, so the phrase taken literally describes such a blonde; the question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means done honestly and openly, with no cheating, as in winning a contest by legitimate means.

clue.text: Conductor in pub facing writer with bad back

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a writing instrument
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A bus conductor in the pub sits opposite an author who has a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests a bus or electricity, but it is the orchestral kind. Sir John Barbirolli led the Hallé Orchestra; Biro is the British everyday word for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Barbirolli was a celebrated British orchestral conductor, long associated with the Hallé in Manchester.

clue.text: Draw cup match

blocks.note: first meaning: a result with equal scores
second meaning: a fixture in a knockout competition

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a single sports report, but a drawn game and a knockout-round fixture are separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an equal result between competitors and, in British usage, a single game in a knockout cup competition.

clue.text: I knew match ground, one in Greater London

indicators.note: something ground is crushed up into bits, so the letters are broken and reassembled

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a game at a sports ground, one somewhere in the London area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match ground' sits together like the name of a stadium, which is apt, but 'ground' is the anagram signal and 'match' part of the fodder. Twickenham is the home of English rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Twickenham is a district of south-west London, within the Greater London area, famous for its national rugby stadium.

clue.text: Stop with fashionable daughter at university

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
in means fashionable, as in the in thing
D is the abbreviation for daughter
in British usage a student is up at university

explanation.surface: A parent is told to call a halt to a stylish daughter's student lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at university is the Oxford-and-Cambridge way of saying in residence, the opposite of being sent down.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind up a meeting or business is to bring it to an end, an idiomatic synonym of stop.

clue.text: Rustic grabbing tail of heath bird

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so one piece closes around another
a tail is the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: last letter of the word
a peasant is a rustic, a country labourer

explanation.surface: A countryman on the heath seizes a bird by its tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rustic' looks like an adjective but is a noun here: a country dweller.
explanation.definitionFit: The pheasant is a long-tailed game bird, commonly reared and shot in the British countryside.

clue.text: Manage following hearing test

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the piece named first in the clue is placed second

blocks.note: a hearing in court is a trial
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Someone copes after taking an audiology check of their ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing test' looks like a single medical phrase, but 'hearing' is a court case and 'test' is the definition. 'Following' puts the manage word after the court word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run is a rehearsal or practice attempt to see whether something works, so it is a kind of test.

clue.text: Beast put in place round ancient city

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece sits around the other

blocks.note: to create is to bring into being or establish
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: An animal is penned up somewhere near the ruins of an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in place' reads as confining the beast, but it means establish, and it wraps around the three-letter city.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature is any living animal, so it is a general synonym for beast.

clue.text: Ban therefore must include male graduate

indicators.note: including something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: ergo is Latin for therefore
M is the abbreviation for male
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A rule is laid down that any exclusion must also cover men with degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The male and graduate pieces sit together after the first letter of ERGO.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade with a particular country, so it is a ban.

clue.text: Pretty sure lad is after rum

blocks.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: Someone is fairly certain that the young man is chasing a drink of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink but is the adjective meaning strange, and 'is after' places the lad behind it rather than pursuing it.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, an odds-on chance is more likely than not to win, so the phrase means very probable.

clue.text: Type of onion: attempt to eat every bit

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: a shot is an attempt, as in have a shot
all means every bit, the whole

explanation.surface: A dare to finish off a whole onion of a particular variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat' fits the onion scene perfectly, but here it tells you the attempt swallows the whole amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small, mild member of the onion family that grows in clusters of bulbs.

clue.text: Fit to eat from deli? Be prepared!

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked over and changed, so the letters are made up anew

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A question about whether the food from a delicatessen is safe, followed by the Scout motto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be prepared!' looks like the Scout motto, but 'prepared' is the anagram signal working on the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible means safe or suitable for eating, the exact sense of fit to eat.

clue.text: Go out with Elizabeth Barrett Browning, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives up its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letters of the poet's three names

explanation.surface: An invitation to go on a date with the Victorian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out with' suggests dating, but 'go out' is the definition, and 'with' only links it to the poet's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: When the tide goes out it ebbs, so the verb means recede or flow away from the shore.

clue.text: German woman with DS, going to court for police department

blocks.note: Frau is German for woman or wife
taken as written
a quad, or quadrangle, is a courtyard

explanation.surface: A German woman accompanies a detective sergeant to court on behalf of the police.
explanation.walkthrough: DS, detective sergeant, fits the police picture but is used here simply as its two letters. 'Court' is a courtyard, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: The fraud squad is the branch of a British police force that investigates financial crime and deception.

clue.text: Star clue

blocks.note: first meaning: the principal role or actor in a show
second meaning: a hint that helps an investigation

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a single phrase, the main hint, but each is a separate meaning of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the principal performer in a play or film and a piece of information detectives follow up.

clue.text: Racehorse ruled out within hour

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in order, so the letters are rearranged
within means inside, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder
HR is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A racehorse is declared a non-runner within the hour before the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruled out' reads as one phrase for a withdrawn runner, but 'out' is the anagram signal on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurdler is a horse trained to race over hurdles, the low jumps used in National Hunt racing.

clue.text: Artist put in account, with electronic printing system

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
a bill is an account of money owed
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: An artist is billed for an electronic printing setup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electronic printing system' reads as one phrase, but 'electronic' just gives E and the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Braille is the writing and printing system of raised dots read by touch, used by blind and partially sighted people.

clue.text: Low, duke creates an atmosphere

blocks.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A gloomy duke brings a heavy feeling into the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like the adjective for downcast, which suits the gloomy scene, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A mood is the prevailing feeling or tone of a place or occasion, the same sense as an atmosphere.

clue.text: Curious deer sent it flying

indicators.note: things set flying are scattered in all directions, so the letters come down in a fresh order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An inquisitive deer knocked something over and sent it tumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' does double work: it is part of the fodder along with the deer and 'it', and 'flying' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being curious about something means wanting to know more about it, the same sense as feeling interested.
